Undoubtedly from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ŕ̥tḱos (“bear”), though it is not exactly clear how the term developed in Italic. Schrijver postulates an Italic sound-law wherein *#HLC- sequences became aLC- in Latin, as perhaps indicated by terms such as argentum (perhaps from *h₂ŕ̥ǵn̥tom), in which case the initial u- is unexpected. However, the linguist Stefan Höfler argues that *#HLC- operated like other *#CLC- sequences, such as mors (< *mr̥t-), in which case *h₂ŕ̥tḱos would develop into *orksos, whence ursus. Schrijver, however, suggests that—even if *#HLC- yielded Latin #oLC-—the outcome ursus…
